newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia oil workers talks to restart Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Colombia oil workers talks to restart Tuesday.

text.p: BOGOTA, May 11 Reuter - Colombia's main oil workers' union will meet with government officials Tuesday in what labor leaders described as a "last-ditch" bid to avoid a strike.
Hernando Hernandez, head of the 7,000-strong USO union, denied media reports over the weekend that the countdown to an all-out stoppage in the state-run oil company Ecopetrol had begun.

Interior Minister Horacio Serpa, meanwhile, said he was optimistic a deal could be reached, thereby removing the threat of a debilitating strike which has been hanging over Ecopetrol since early December.
"There will be a meeting Tuesday evening in a last-ditch effort to reach a final accord," Hernandez told the Radionet radio network Sunday.
"The government must show a more flexible position if it wants to avert this strike," he added.

The USO union has been bogged down in collective contract talks with Ecopetrol officials and government officials since January. The negotiations were preceded by a union threat to declare an all-out strike if Ecopetrol went ahead with plans for what it claimed was the "creeping privatization" of the state-run oil sector.

The main bone of contention continues to be plans for the future of Ecopetrol's natural gas operations. Ecopetrol originally favored hiving off gas operations to an independent company financed by the private and public sector.
It is now pressing for the creation of an autonomous state-owned company, to be called Ecogas. The USO union, however, argues that the company should be a subsidiary of Ecopetrol.
"Taking national interest into account above everything else, then I think we can reach an agreement and avoid the trauma of a strike," Serpa told Radionet.
The talks are scheduled to take place in Bogota at 1800 local time/2300 GMT Tuesday.
